Schema accounts

Tables

accounts.account

table · Account

A customer account: the party that owns data and activity in the system. Accounts are soft-deleted and can be merged into another account.

#ColumnTypeNullDefaultKeysDescription
1iduuidnopublic.uuid_generate_v7()PKThe surrogate key, a time-ordered UUID (version 7) generated by the database.
See also: public.uuid_generate_v7
2namecitextyesThe account's display name. Case-insensitive.
Business name: Account Name
Example: Contoso Ltd
3descriptioncitextyesFree-text notes about the account.
4is_deletedbooleannofalseSoft-delete flag. A deleted row is kept for history and ignored by normal queries; see deleted_utc.
5is_activebooleannotrueWhether the row is in use. An inactive row is kept but not offered for new work.
6merged_with_account_iduuidyesFKThe account this one was merged into. Null for an account that has not been merged.
References accounts.account(id).
See also: accounts.account.id
7created_principal_iduuidnoFKThe principal that created the row.
References accounts.account(id).
See also: identity.principal.id
8created_utctimestampnopublic.utc_now()When the row was created, in UTC. Set by the database.
Example: 2026-10-09 14:03:00
9updated_principal_iduuidnoFKThe principal that last changed the row. Equal to created_principal_id until the first change.
References accounts.account(id).
See also: identity.principal.id
10updated_utctimestampnopublic.utc_now()When the row was last changed, in UTC. Equal to created_utc until the first change.
Example: 2026-10-09 14:03:00
11deleted_principal_iduuidyesFKThe principal that soft-deleted the row. Null while the row is not deleted.
References accounts.account(id).
See also: identity.principal.id
12deleted_utctimestampyesWhen the row was soft-deleted, in UTC. Null while the row is not deleted.
Example: 2026-10-09 14:03:00

billing.invoice

table · Invoice

A bill for an account covering one billing period. Created as a draft with its lines by billing.run_billing_cycle, then opened for payment.

#ColumnTypeNullDefaultKeysDescription
1iduuidnopublic.uuid_generate_v7()PKThe surrogate key, a time-ordered UUID (version 7) generated by the database.
2invoice_numbertextnobilling.next_invoice_number()UKThe number printed on the invoice. Unique.
Example: INV-005001
3account_iduuidnoFKThe account being billed.
References accounts.account(id).
See also: accounts.account.id
4subscription_iduuidyesFKThe subscription the invoice is for. Null for a one-off invoice.
References billing.subscription(id).
See also: billing.subscription.id

6period_startdatenoFirst day covered by the invoice.
7period_enddatenoDay the covered period ends. Exclusive.

Generated: subtotal + tax_total.

Views

billing.v_invoice_aging

view

Open invoices (issued, not yet paid) with how many days past due they are and the aging bucket they fall in: current, 1-30, 31-60, or 61+ days overdue.

ColumnTypeDescription
invoice_iduuid
invoice_numbertext
account_iduuid
account_namecitext
totalpg_catalog.numeric
due_ondate
days_overdue
aging_bucket
SELECT i.id AS invoice_id,
       i.invoice_number,
       i.account_id,
       a.name AS account_name,
       i.total,
       i.due_on,
       greatest(current_date - i.due_on, 0) AS days_overdue,
       CASE
           WHEN i.due_on >= current_date THEN 'current'
           WHEN current_date - i.due_on <= 30 THEN '1-30'
           WHEN current_date - i.due_on <= 60 THEN '31-60'
           ELSE '61+'
       END AS aging_bucket
FROM billing.invoice AS i
JOIN accounts.account AS a ON a.id = i.account_id
WHERE i.status = 'open'

billing.v_subscription_current

view

The live subscriptions (trialing, active, or past due) with the account and plan, the days until renewal, the plan price as a monthly figure, and the usage reported so far this period against the plan allowance.

ColumnTypeDescription
subscription_iduuid
account_iduuid
account_namecitext
plan_codecitext
plan_namecitext
statusbilling.subscription_status
current_period_startdate
current_period_enddate
days_until_renewal
cancel_at_period_endpg_catalog.bool
monthly_equivalent_price
usage_this_period
included_unitspg_catalog.int4
SELECT s.id AS subscription_id,
       s.account_id,
       a.name AS account_name,
       pl.code AS plan_code,
       pl.name AS plan_name,
       s.status,
       s.current_period_start,
       s.current_period_end,
       s.current_period_end - current_date AS days_until_renewal,
       s.cancel_at_period_end,
       CASE pl.billing_interval
           WHEN 'month' THEN pl.price
           WHEN 'year'  THEN round(pl.price / 12, 2)
       END AS monthly_equivalent_price,
       billing.usage_in_period(s.id, s.current_period_start, s.current_period_end) AS usage_this_period,
       pl.included_units
FROM billing.subscription AS s
JOIN billing.plan AS pl ON pl.id = s.plan_id
JOIN accounts.account AS a ON a.id = s.account_id
WHERE s.status IN ('trialing', 'active', 'past_due')

Functions and procedures

billing.invoice_line_changed()

function

Trigger function for billing.invoice_line: after a line is added, removed, or changed, sets the invoice subtotal to the sum of its line amounts.

invoice_line_changed() returns trigger

Language: plpgsql

billing.next_invoice_number()

function

The next invoice number, such as INV-005001. The default for billing.invoice.invoice_number.

  • See also: billing.invoice_number_seq

next_invoice_number() returns text

Language: sql

billing.period_end(date, billing.billing_interval)

function

The exclusive end of a billing period that starts on the given date: one month or one year later.

  • Example: select billing.period_end('2026-01-31', 'month') -- 2026-02-28

period_end(p_period_start date, p_interval billing.billing_interval) returns date

Language: sql · Volatility: immutable

billing.prorate(numeric, date, date, date)

function

The part of a period charge that applies from a change date to the end of the period, by days. Used to credit the unused part of the old plan and charge the new one when a subscription changes mid-period. A change date outside the period is clamped to it.

  • Example: select billing.prorate(30.00, '2026-06-01', '2026-07-01', '2026-06-16') -- 15.00

prorate(p_amount numeric, p_period_start date, p_period_end date, p_change_on date) returns numeric

Language: sql · Volatility: immutable

billing.run_billing_cycle(date, uuid)

procedure

Bills every live subscription whose current period has ended by the given date. For each one it raises an open invoice with the plan fee and any usage beyond the plan allowance, stamps the usage events it billed, and then renews the subscription for the next period, or cancels it if it was set to cancel at period end. Subscriptions still in a free trial are rolled forward without an invoice.

Commits after each subscription, so it must be called outside a transaction block.

  • Example: call billing.run_billing_cycle(current_date, '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002')

run_billing_cycle(p_as_of date, p_principal_id uuid)

Language: plpgsql

billing.usage_in_period(uuid, date, date)

function

Total usage units reported for a subscription from the start date (inclusive) to the end date (exclusive), whether or not they have been billed.

usage_in_period(p_subscription_id uuid, p_period_start date, p_period_end date) returns bigint

Language: sql · Volatility: stable

Views

catalog.v_category_tree

view

The category hierarchy flattened with a recursive query: each category with its depth (0 for a root), its full path, its root, and how many active products sit directly in it. Rows are in tree order.

ColumnTypeDescription
id
parent_category_id
root_category_id
code
name
depth
path
active_product_count
WITH RECURSIVE tree AS (
    SELECT c.id,
           c.parent_category_id,
           c.id AS root_category_id,
           c.code,
           c.name,
           c.sort_order,
           0 AS depth,
           c.name::text AS path,
           ARRAY[c.sort_order, 0] AS sort_key
    FROM catalog.category AS c
    WHERE c.parent_category_id IS NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT c.id,
           c.parent_category_id,
           t.root_category_id,
           c.code,
           c.name,
           c.sort_order,
           t.depth + 1,
           t.path || ' > ' || c.name::text,
           t.sort_key || c.sort_order
    FROM catalog.category AS c
    JOIN tree AS t ON t.id = c.parent_category_id
)
SELECT t.id,
       t.parent_category_id,
       t.root_category_id,
       t.code,
       t.name,
       t.depth,
       t.path,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM catalog.product AS p WHERE p.category_id = t.id AND p.is_active) AS active_product_count
FROM tree AS t
ORDER BY t.sort_key, t.path

catalog.v_product_availability

view

Every active product with the stock it has across active warehouses: units on hand, how many warehouses hold it, whether any is in stock, and whether the total has fallen to the combined reorder points.

ColumnTypeDescription
product_id
sku
name
category_path
unit_price
quantity_on_hand
warehouse_count
is_in_stock
needs_reorder
SELECT p.id AS product_id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       catalog.category_path(p.category_id) AS category_path,
       p.unit_price,
       coalesce(s.quantity_on_hand, 0) AS quantity_on_hand,
       coalesce(s.warehouse_count, 0) AS warehouse_count,
       coalesce(s.quantity_on_hand, 0) > 0 AS is_in_stock,
       coalesce(s.quantity_on_hand, 0) <= coalesce(s.reorder_point, 0) AS needs_reorder
FROM catalog.product AS p
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT sl.product_id,
           sum(sl.quantity_on_hand)::integer AS quantity_on_hand,
           sum(sl.reorder_point)::integer AS reorder_point,
           count(*)::integer AS warehouse_count
    FROM inventory.stock_level AS sl
    JOIN inventory.warehouse AS w ON w.id = sl.warehouse_id AND w.is_active
    GROUP BY sl.product_id
) AS s ON s.product_id = p.id
WHERE p.is_active

Functions and procedures

inventory.apply_stock_movement()

function

Trigger function for inventory.stock_movement: applies each new movement to the stock_level row for its product and warehouse, creating the row on first use. A movement that would take stock below zero fails on the stock_level check constraint, which rolls the movement back.

apply_stock_movement() returns trigger

Language: plpgsql

Schema reporting

Views

reporting.mv_customer_lifetime_value

materialized view

One row per customer with their order count, lifetime spend, and first and last order dates, counting orders that were placed and not cancelled or refunded. Customers who have not ordered have a count of zero. Refresh with reporting.refresh_materialized_views.

ColumnTypeDescription
customer_iduuid
display_namecitext
account_iduuid
order_count
lifetime_value
first_order_utc
last_order_utc
SELECT c.id AS customer_id,
       c.display_name,
       c.account_id,
       count(oh.id)::integer AS order_count,
       coalesce(sum(oh.total), 0) AS lifetime_value,
       min(oh.placed_utc) AS first_order_utc,
       max(oh.placed_utc) AS last_order_utc
FROM sales.customer AS c
LEFT JOIN sales.order_header AS oh
       ON oh.customer_id = c.id
      AND oh.status IN ('placed', 'paid', 'shipped', 'delivered')
GROUP BY c.id, c.display_name, c.account_id

reporting.mv_daily_sales

materialized view

Sales per day for orders that were placed and not cancelled or refunded: order count, units, gross sales, discounts, net revenue, and average order value. Refresh with reporting.refresh_materialized_views.

ColumnTypeDescription
sale_date
order_count
units_sold
gross_sales
discounts
net_revenue
average_order_value
SELECT oh.placed_utc::date AS sale_date,
       count(*)::integer AS order_count,
       sum(u.unit_count)::integer AS units_sold,
       sum(oh.subtotal) AS gross_sales,
       sum(oh.discount_total) AS discounts,
       sum(oh.total) AS net_revenue,
       round(avg(oh.total), 2) AS average_order_value
FROM sales.order_header AS oh
JOIN (
    SELECT ol.order_id, sum(ol.quantity) AS unit_count
    FROM sales.order_line AS ol
    GROUP BY ol.order_id
) AS u ON u.order_id = oh.id
WHERE oh.status IN ('placed', 'paid', 'shipped', 'delivered')
GROUP BY oh.placed_utc::date

reporting.mv_low_stock

materialized view

Active products whose stock across active warehouses has fallen to or below their combined reorder points, with how far short they are. The purchasing worklist. Refresh with reporting.refresh_materialized_views.

ColumnTypeDescription
product_iduuid
skucitext
namecitext
quantity_on_hand
reorder_point
shortfall
SELECT p.id AS product_id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       sum(sl.quantity_on_hand)::integer AS quantity_on_hand,
       sum(sl.reorder_point)::integer AS reorder_point,
       (sum(sl.reorder_point) - sum(sl.quantity_on_hand))::integer AS shortfall
FROM inventory.stock_level AS sl
JOIN inventory.warehouse AS w ON w.id = sl.warehouse_id AND w.is_active
JOIN catalog.product AS p ON p.id = sl.product_id AND p.is_active
GROUP BY p.id, p.sku, p.name
HAVING sum(sl.quantity_on_hand) <= sum(sl.reorder_point)

reporting.mv_monthly_recurring_revenue

materialized view

Monthly recurring revenue per plan: the live (active or past-due) subscriptions on it and what they bring in each month, with yearly plans divided by twelve. Trials are not counted. Refresh with reporting.refresh_materialized_views.

ColumnTypeDescription
plan_iduuid
plan_codecitext
plan_namecitext
subscription_count
mrr
SELECT pl.id AS plan_id,
       pl.code AS plan_code,
       pl.name AS plan_name,
       count(s.id)::integer AS subscription_count,
       coalesce(sum(
           CASE pl.billing_interval
               WHEN 'month' THEN pl.price
               WHEN 'year'  THEN round(pl.price / 12, 2)
           END
       ) FILTER (WHERE s.id IS NOT NULL), 0) AS mrr
FROM billing.plan AS pl
LEFT JOIN billing.subscription AS s
       ON s.plan_id = pl.id
      AND s.status IN ('active', 'past_due')
GROUP BY pl.id, pl.code, pl.name

reporting.mv_top_products

materialized view

Products ranked by revenue across all orders that were placed and not cancelled or refunded, with units sold. Refresh with reporting.refresh_materialized_views.

ColumnTypeDescription
product_id
sku
name
units_sold
revenue
revenue_rank
SELECT ranked.product_id,
       ranked.sku,
       ranked.name,
       ranked.units_sold,
       ranked.revenue,
       rank() OVER (ORDER BY ranked.revenue DESC) AS revenue_rank
FROM (
    SELECT p.id AS product_id,
           p.sku,
           p.name,
           sum(ol.quantity)::integer AS units_sold,
           sum(ol.line_total) AS revenue
    FROM sales.order_line AS ol
    JOIN sales.order_header AS oh ON oh.id = ol.order_id
    JOIN catalog.product AS p ON p.id = ol.product_id
    WHERE oh.status IN ('placed', 'paid', 'shipped', 'delivered')
    GROUP BY p.id, p.sku, p.name
) AS ranked

Views

sales.v_order_summary

view

One row per order with its customer, line and unit counts, totals, captured payments, and the balance still due. The main query for order lists and customer service.

ColumnTypeDescription
order_id
order_number
status
customer_id
customer_name
customer_email
line_count
unit_count
subtotal
discount_total
tax_total
shipping_total
total
paid_amount
balance_due
placed_utc
created_utc
SELECT oh.id AS order_id,
       oh.order_number,
       oh.status,
       c.id AS customer_id,
       c.display_name AS customer_name,
       c.email AS customer_email,
       coalesce(l.line_count, 0) AS line_count,
       coalesce(l.unit_count, 0) AS unit_count,
       oh.subtotal,
       oh.discount_total,
       oh.tax_total,
       oh.shipping_total,
       oh.total,
       coalesce(p.paid_amount, 0) AS paid_amount,
       oh.total - coalesce(p.paid_amount, 0) AS balance_due,
       oh.placed_utc,
       oh.created_utc
FROM sales.order_header AS oh
JOIN sales.customer AS c ON c.id = oh.customer_id
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT ol.order_id, count(*)::integer AS line_count, sum(ol.quantity)::integer AS unit_count
    FROM sales.order_line AS ol
    GROUP BY ol.order_id
) AS l ON l.order_id = oh.id
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT pay.order_id, sum(pay.amount) AS paid_amount
    FROM sales.payment AS pay
    WHERE pay.status = 'captured'
    GROUP BY pay.order_id
) AS p ON p.order_id = oh.id

Functions and procedures

sales.apply_discount_code(uuid, text, uuid)

procedure

Applies a discount code to a draft order and recomputes its totals. Fails if the code is unknown, inactive, expired, used up, or does not reduce this order (for example the subtotal is below its minimum).

apply_discount_code(p_order_id uuid, p_code text, p_principal_id uuid)

Language: plpgsql

sales.cancel_order(uuid, uuid, text)

procedure

Cancels an order that has not shipped: returns its stock to the warehouses it came from, marks captured payments refunded, gives back the discount code use, and moves the order to cancelled. An order that has shipped fails on the status guard trigger and nothing is changed.

cancel_order(p_order_id uuid, p_principal_id uuid, p_reason text)

Language: plpgsql

sales.discount_amount(uuid, numeric, timestamp)

function

How much a discount code takes off a subtotal at a point in time: the percentage or fixed amount, never more than the subtotal. Zero when the code is unknown, inactive, outside its validity window, or the subtotal is below its minimum.

discount_amount(p_discount_code_id uuid, p_subtotal numeric, p_at timestamp) returns money_amount

Language: sql · Volatility: stable

sales.guard_order_line_change()

function

Trigger function for sales.order_line: rejects adding, removing, or changing the product, quantity, or price of a line once its order has left draft.

guard_order_line_change() returns trigger

Language: plpgsql

sales.guard_order_status()

function

Trigger function for sales.order_header: rejects a status change that is not allowed by sales.is_valid_order_transition and stamps the timestamp that goes with the new status.

guard_order_status() returns trigger

Language: plpgsql

sales.is_valid_order_transition(sales.order_status, sales.order_status)

function

Whether an order may move from one status to another. Cancelled and refunded are final.

draft -> placed -> paid -> shipped -> delivered, with cancel allowed until the order ships and refund allowed after.

is_valid_order_transition(p_from sales.order_status, p_to sales.order_status) returns boolean

Language: sql · Volatility: immutable

sales.next_order_number()

function

The next human-readable order number, such as SO-100042. The default for sales.order_header.order_number.

  • See also: sales.order_number_seq

next_order_number() returns text

Language: sql

sales.order_balance(uuid)

function

What a customer still owes on an order: the order total less its captured payments. Null for an unknown order.

order_balance(p_order_id uuid) returns numeric

Language: sql · Volatility: stable

sales.order_line_changed()

function

Trigger function for sales.order_line: after a line is added, removed, or repriced, refreshes the totals on its order.

order_line_changed() returns trigger

Language: plpgsql

sales.place_order(uuid, uuid)

procedure

Places a draft order: takes the stock for every line out of the warehouses (one inventory.stock_movement per warehouse used), counts the discount code use, and moves the order to placed. All or nothing: if any line cannot be filled, nothing is changed.

  • Example: call sales.place_order('018f...', '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002')

place_order(p_order_id uuid, p_principal_id uuid)

Language: plpgsql

sales.record_order_status()

function

Trigger function for sales.order_header: writes a sales.order_status_history row when an order is created and each time its status changes, attributed to the principal that made the change.

record_order_status() returns trigger

Language: plpgsql

sales.record_payment(uuid, sales.payment_method, numeric, text, uuid)

procedure

Records a captured payment against a placed order and, when the payments cover the order total, moves the order to paid. Rejects a payment larger than the balance still owed.

record_payment(p_order_id uuid, p_method sales.payment_method, p_amount numeric, p_external_reference text, p_principal_id uuid)

Language: plpgsql

sales.refresh_order_totals(uuid)

function

Recomputes an order's subtotal, discount, tax, and shipping from its lines and discount code. Called by the order_line_totals trigger and by sales.apply_discount_code.

refresh_order_totals(p_order_id uuid) returns void

Language: plpgsql

sales.shipping_charge(numeric)

function

The shipping charge for an order subtotal: a flat 7.50, free from 100.00, and nothing for an empty order.

shipping_charge(p_subtotal numeric) returns money_amount

Language: sql · Volatility: immutable
